intro: You are standing before Mama Hatun Tomb, in Erzincan province, from the late 12th century. It was built for the Saltukid ruler Mama Hatun, and it stands at the centre of a circular walled court, a plan with no other example in Anatolia.
history: The tomb at Tercan in Erzincan was built at the end of the twelfth century for Mama Hatun, ruler of the Saltukids. It stands at the exact centre of a circular walled court with eight niches, and you enter through a single portal. This plan is repeated nowhere else in Anatolian Turkish architecture.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the circular court wall, the eight niches, the portal and the fluted cap.
facts: Did you know? Mama Hatun was one of the few women in Anatolia to rule a state and strike coins in her own name. And her tomb stands at the centre of a circular walled court, a plan repeated nowhere else in Anatolian Turkish architecture.
outro: This brings our tour of Mama Hatun Tomb to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
